Jurong East MRT Station is a crucial integrated transport hub in western Singapore, currently connecting the North-South Line and East-West Line. It will also connect to the Jurong Region Line in the future, serving commuters, businesses, and residential areas.

To give you a quick overview, here's a summary of its key information:

Basic Information

· Station Code: NS1/EW24 (future JE5)

· Operational Status: Opened November 5, 1988; the Jurong Region Line is expected to open in 2028.

· Line Type: North-South Line terminus & East-West Line interchange station

· Station Structure: Elevated station (both current and future lines are elevated)

Station Layout and Transfers
Jurong East Station boasts a unique design, being the only elevated station in Singapore with three island platforms (6 platform faces in total). This design is intended to efficiently handle the massive transfer passenger flow.

• East-West Line (EWL): Runs east-west through Singapore, providing access to Pasir Ris and Tuas Link.

• North-South Line (NSL): Terminates here, heading towards Marina South Pier.

• Platform Usage: To improve efficiency, platforms A and B are only open during weekday morning and evening peak hours. At other times, please use platforms C to F.

Station Exits and Surrounding Facilities: Jurong East Station is seamlessly connected to surrounding buildings via a network of covered walkways (such as the J-Walk).

• Exit A: Primarily leads to Jurong East Centre, Jurong Regional Library, Science Centre, etc.

• Exit B: Connects to Jurong East Bus Interchange and Jurong Town Hall Bus Interchange, allowing transfers to cross-border buses to Johor Bahru, Malaysia.

• Exits C/D: Located on the second floor, directly connected to JEM, Westgate Shopping Centre, Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, etc. via the J-Walk corridor.

Transportation Connections

• Buses: Two large bus interchanges are located next to the station (Jurong East and Jurong Town Hall), with extensive route coverage.

• Others: Taxi stands and private car pick-up/drop-off points are available at the station.

Future Plans
The Jurong Regional Line (JRL) is expected to connect to this station in 2028. At that time, it will further enhance regional connectivity in western Singapore, making Jurong East Station a hub for three MRT lines.

🛍️ Major Nearby Landmarks

From the station, you can easily reach the following locations:

• Large Shopping Malls: JEM, Westgate, IMM Outlets

• Medical Facilities: Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, Jurong Community Hospital

• Business Districts: International Business Park, Jurong Business District.

• Public Facilities: Jurong Regional Library, Singapore Science Centre.

🚇 Travel Tips

• Avoid Peak Hours: This station is extremely busy during morning and evening rush hours. If possible, try to travel during off-peak times.

• Platform Notice: As mentioned earlier, platforms A and B are only open during weekday peak hours. Please pay attention to station announcements and signs before traveling.

• Utilize the Covered Walkways: The station connects to several nearby shopping malls and hospitals via covered walkways (J-Walk), allowing for comfortable passage even in rainy weather.

It is the terminus for the North South Line. It is located at the heart of the Jurong Lake District, within the vicinity of JCube, Jem, Westgate, IMM, Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and Jurong East Bus Interchange.

The train station had both the North- south line and the Éast- west line, which covers many parts of Singapore. There are times when one would make choices of taking a morning rejuvenating jog, to do a workout at a gym, play a game of football with buddies, or to take a sun setting stroll with family members to enjoy a cool breezy evening. Well... Bukit Gombak park, the Little Guilin, built within the vicinity where there's easy access to public transportation of MRT and buses enable even neighbouring towns to drop by for a healthy activity.

If one were to embark upon an intellectual pilgrimage through the hallowed terrain of Singapore’s urban tapestry, few locales induce as much bewildered reverence as the legendary Bukit Gombak—a district whose name alone evokes both mystique and the faint sound of an uncle coughing in the distance.

From the moment one steps foot upon this storied soil, an overwhelming sense of “Ah… so this is it ah?” floods the senses. It is a place where the ordinary becomes extraordinary, not by divine intent, but by sheer, stubborn idiosyncrasy.

---

The Meteorological Madness

The climate of Bukit Gombak deserves its own National Day Parade segment. The heat here is no mere warmth—it is an omnidirectional thermodynamic assault. One does not simply sweat; one exudes moisture like a malfunctioning humidifier undergoing a midlife crisis.

Stand still for five minutes and you will experience all three stages of evaporation, condensation, and emotional breakdown.

---

The Vehicular Symphony

The roads of Bukit Gombak host an eclectic assemblage of vehicles, each contributing to a soundscape best described as “orchestra of slightly frustrated car owners.”

Between the roaring motorcycles, honking cars, and the occasional auntie yelling “OI LOOK OUT LAH”, one cannot help but marvel at the cacophony. It is as though every driver is participating in an unspoken competition for the prestigious Loudest Possible Engine at 8am award.

---

The Architectural Aesthetic

The HDB blocks tower with a quiet dignity, each painted in a shade that can only be described as “existential beige.” They gaze upon you as if whispering,
“Yes… we have seen things. Mostly people doing their laundry.”

The nearby factories complete the picture, standing proudly like metallic monoliths of productivity and mild respiratory discomfort.

---

Recreational Offerings: A Study in Contrast

The iconic Little Guilin sits resplendent, a serene oasis surrounded by lush greenery and calm waters—a tranquil marvel that inspires peace, reflection, and the occasional influencer photoshoot featuring suspiciously dramatic poses.

But venture just thirty seconds away and you are greeted with the unmistakable scent of industrial enthusiasm, reminding you that serenity is but a mere visitor here, not a permanent resident.

Final Verdict

Bukit Gombak is a paradoxical marvel—a tapestry woven with threads of heat, honking, and heartfelt community spirit. It is  chaotic and terrible, filled with anger and gloom.

Opened on 10 March 1990 as part of the Branch line of the East West MRT line between Jurong East and Choa Chu Kang, and this MRT line was incorporated to the extended North-South MRT line on 10 February 1996 when the Woodlands MRT Extension first opened. Its station code was B2 before being changed to its present form, NS3 in 2001. The station is located in Bukit Batok Central planning subzone at Bukit Batok West Avenue 5 near the junction with Bukit Batok East Avenue 5, bringing direct rail connectivity to serve Bukit Gombak Stadium, Bukit Gombak Neighbourhood Centre, Bukit Gombak Sports Hall and Bukit Batok Town Park (also known as Little Guilin). The bus services serving Bukit Gombak MRT station are Tower Transit feeder bus service 945 between Bukit Batok Bus Interchange and Bukit Batok Street 34, SMRT Buses trunk service 991 between Bukit Batok Bus Interchange and Choa Chu Kang Bus Interchange and the free shuttle bus service which connects this MRT station to HillV2 shopping mall in Hillview.

Singapore's MRT (Mass Rapid Transit)
When visiting Singapore, traveling by subway is a significantly cost-effective and convenient way to explore the Lion City. Furthermore, visitors have the opportunity to experience one of Southeast Asia's most modern subway systems.

Note:
- You can use the MRT EZ-link card for public transport: Subway (MRT) and buses in Singapore.

- Due to the policy prioritizing public transport, if you travel continuously by MRT followed by a bus and vice versa, the fare for the next leg of your journey will be significantly reduced (the system automatically deducts the fare from your trip).
- If your MRT card runs out of money, you can top it up at the machines at the stations using Cash (Singapore Dollars) or Coins. Please note that you should use denominations of S$5 or S$10 (do not use denominations that are too small or too large).
- The MRT card is valid for 5 years (EZ-link card), so you can lend it to friends after purchase or give it away for reuse.
- To be proactive in your journey, you should get a Singapore map at the airport that has an MRT map available.
- For first-time travelers or those unfamiliar with the route, it is advisable to stand near the exit because the door displays the location of the train, the next station, etc., for easy reference. Some older trains only have static maps (not showing the location). - Therefore, you must listen to announcements or look along the carriage for LED lights displaying the next station.

- Train fares will be automatically deducted from your MRT card account. If your card balance is below $2, the system will require you to top up.

- Eating, smoking, and drinking are strictly prohibited on public transport in Singapore and will result in a minimum fine of approximately S$250 if caught.

- You can easily explore Singapore on your own using the MRT public transport.

- To find your arrival and departure stations, please check the end points, as the train direction signs at the stations will indicate the train's destination (see the map below or a tourist map for the stops).

- At each station, there are signs and train route maps (standing posts near the stairs).

- Because the train schedule is very frequent, you shouldn't rush; take your time to explore and discover (maximum 10 minutes, many stops are longer). The trains are only 2 minutes apart.

Kranji MRT station is a convenient and well-maintained transit point that serves commuters traveling between northern Singapore and the rest of Singapore. The station is especially valued for its practical layout, clean surroundings, and smooth passenger flow, making daily travel comfortable and efficient for both residents and visitors.
One of the station’s strongest advantages is its accessibility. It is strategically located near important facilities, checkpoints, and industrial areas, making it a key stop for workers, students, and travelers. Signage inside the station is clear and easy to follow, which helps first-time users navigate without confusion. Ticketing machines, gantries, and platforms are arranged logically, so even during peak hours movement remains relatively smooth and organized.
Passengers often appreciate the station’s cleanliness and orderly environment. The platforms are spacious and well-ventilated, and safety markings are clearly visible. Staff presence and surveillance systems contribute to a secure atmosphere, giving commuters peace of mind while waiting for trains. The surrounding area is also straightforward to navigate, with bus connections and taxi points located nearby for easy transfers.
Another positive aspect is the calm and less crowded feel compared to major interchange stations. Many commuters find this refreshing, especially during morning and evening travel, as it allows for a more relaxed commuting experience. The station’s simple design and functional layout reflect efficiency rather than complexity, which many users prefer.
Overall, Kranji MRT station is a reliable, commuter-friendly transit stop that offers convenience, cleanliness, and accessibility. While it may not be the busiest or most glamorous station, its practicality and smooth operations make it an important and appreciated part of Singapore’s public transport network.

Admiralty MRT (NS10) is an elevated station on Singapore's North-South Line (NSL) in the heart of Woodlands, known for its seamless integration with Kampung Admiralty, an innovative senior-focused development featuring housing, a medical centre, and a hawker centre. It serves as a vital transport hub connecting residents via MRT and bus to the city and other parts of Singapore, offering amenities like shops and food options within its premises and nearby Causeway Point, reflecting the area's transition from a former naval base to a modern, family-friendly hub.
Key Features:
Line: North-South Line (NSL).
Operator: SMRT Corporation.
Structure: Elevated, with two tracks and two platforms.
Connectivity: Excellent links to Woodlands, Yishun, and the Central area; near expressways (SLE, BKE).
Accessibility: Wheelchair accessible with bicycle facilities.
Notable Integrations:
Kampung Admiralty: Directly linked, this unique vertical village combines public housing for seniors with a medical centre, childcare, and a hawker centre.
Causeway Point: A major shopping mall adjacent to the station, offering extensive retail and dining.

Opened on 10 February 1996 as part of the Woodlands extension of the North-South MRT line, it is one of the three above-ground North-South MRT line stations in Woodlands New Town, the other two being Marsiling and Woodlands MRT stations. Its station code was N15 before being changed to its present form, NS10 in 2001. The station is located in Admiralty planning subzone at Woodlands Avenue 7 near the junction with Woodlands Avenue 6 and Woodlands Drive 71, bringing direct rail connectivity to serve the residential areas east of Woodlands Town Centre (Neighbourhoods 6 and 7), Admiralty Place, Kampung Admiralty, Woodlands Galaxy Community Club, Greenwood Primary School, Admiralty Primary School, Woodlands Admiral Garden, Circle Green Park, MINDS Woodlands Gardens School, Woodlands Ring Secondary School and Woodlands East Neighbourhood Police Centre. The station was named after a former British Naval Base which was located at the northern coast of Singapore, which was fairly far away from Admiralty MRT station and was closer to Sembawang at that time. The bus services serving Admiralty MRT station are SMRT Buses bus services 901M, 904, 912, 912A, 913 (east loop) and 964 and Tower Transit Singapore bus services 965, 965A and 969 (along Woodlands Avenue 7) and SMRT Buses services 962 and 962C (along Woodlands Avenue 6) as well as shuttle bus services to and from Singapore Safety Driving Centre (SSDC) and Sembawang Shopping Centre (Friday to Sunday and Public Holidays only).

My email to SMRT today..

Dear Customer Relations Team,

I am writing to raise a concern regarding an incident reported to us by my brother that occurred on 21 December at approximately 2.10–2.15 pm at Sembawang MRT station.

According to my brother, he observed an elderly man using his mobile phone to zoom in on and take photographs of two females who were standing near the station map area. The conduct appeared targeted rather than incidental.

My brother informed one of the station staff members at the baggage check area on what happened, and suggested that they look into the matter. However, he was told that because the incident occurred in a public area, it was acceptable, unless the individual was pointing the phone at a specific person. My brother again clarified that the man had indeed zoomed in and directed his phone towards the two females.

I am extremely concerned both about the incident itself and the response given by the staff member. While photography in public spaces may not always be unlawful, targeted or intrusive photography particularly when zooming in on individuals warrant intervention or at least monitoring.

I would appreciate it if the station could:

1. Review the incident, including any available CCTV footage from the relevant time and location; and

2. Reinforce guidance to frontline staff on how to respond appropriately when members of the public report potentially intrusive or concerning behavior.

The intention of this email is to ensure commuter/public safety and to prevent similar or more serious incidents from occurring in the future.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

Yishun MRT Station, located on Singapore’s North-South Line (Red Line), is one of the most convenient and well-connected MRT stations in the northern region. Whether you’re commuting daily or just visiting the area, Yishun MRT offers excellent accessibility and a smooth travel experience.

One of the standout features of Yishun MRT is its strategic location. Just next to the station is the large and popular Northpoint City Mall, which makes this area a vibrant hub of shopping, dining, and services. The mall has a wide variety of retail outlets, supermarkets, food courts, restaurants, electronics shops, fashion stores, and essential services like banks, clinics, and salons—all within walking distance from the station.

Right outside the MRT station is the Yishun Bus Interchange, which connects to many bus routes across Singapore. This makes it extremely convenient for commuters to transfer between MRT and bus services with ease. Whether you’re heading to other parts of the North, or travelling toward the city, Yishun serves as a great starting point or transfer hub.

The station itself is clean, well-maintained, and safe, with helpful signage and barrier-free access for elderly and wheelchair users. During peak hours, it gets quite busy, but the crowd is managed well.

In terms of convenience, everything you need is nearby—groceries, food, retail shopping, public transport, and even community facilities. It’s an ideal location for residents and visitors alike.

Overall, Yishun MRT Station is not just a transport node—it’s a central hub for lifestyle and daily needs in the northern part of Singapore. If you’re looking for easy commuting with all amenities nearby, this is one of the best-connected and most practical MRT stations in the city.

Toa Payoh MRT Station (NS19) is a key station on Singapore's North-South Line, located in the central region of the island. Opened on November 7, 1987, it is one of Singapore’s oldest MRT stations and the first to feature an integrated bus interchange, reflecting a pioneering step in seamless public transport connectivity. Situated in the heart of Toa Payoh, the station serves a vibrant residential and commercial area, including landmarks like Toa Payoh Town Park, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, and nearby schools. The station's design incorporates simple yet functional architecture, with easy access for commuters, including elevators, escalators, and barrier-free facilities. It continues to play a vital role in Singapore’s transit network.

Opened on 12 December 1987 as part of the first phase of the MRT system along with Novena, Newton, Orchard, Dhoby Ghaut, City Hall and Raffles Place stations on the North South MRT Line (NSL) as well as Tanjong Pagar and Outram Park stations on the East West MRT Line (EWL), the station is one of the three MRT stations located along the popular shopping belt in Singapore, Orchard Road. Its station code was N2 before being changed to its present form, NS23 in 2001. Exit B of this station was heavily renovated from January 2007 to July 2009 to make way for 313@Somerset while Exits C and D were opened on 25 April 2014 in conjunction with the opening of Orchard Gateway. This station is conveniently located near Comcentre, Singapore Power Building, Skate Park, 313@Somerset, Orchard Gateway, Orchard Central, Cathay Cineleisure Orchard, Centrepoint Shopping Centre, Mandarin Orchard, The Heeren, Faber House, Orchard Point, Peranakan Place and Emerald Hill. Formerly known as Killiney, it was renamed as Somerset in November 1982.

Dhoby Ghaut MRT Station is a prominent underground interchange station in Singapore, uniquely serving three major MRT lines: the North South Line (NSL), North East Line (NEL), and Circle Line (CCL). This strategic connectivity makes it an essential hub for commuters and tourists alike. ￼

Accessibility:

Situated beneath the eastern end of Orchard Road, the station boasts multiple entrances and exits that seamlessly connect to surrounding landmarks. Notably, it provides direct access to Plaza Singapura, a popular shopping mall, and is integrated with The Atrium@Orchard commercial development . ￼

Nearby Attractions:
•	Plaza Singapura: A comprehensive shopping destination offering a variety of retail and dining options .
•	The Istana: The official residence of Singapore’s President, located nearby.
•	National Museum of Singapore: A short walk away, this museum offers insights into Singapore’s rich history .
•	Dhoby Ghaut Green: An urban park providing a serene environment amidst the bustling city . ￼

Facilities:

The station is equipped with amenities to enhance commuter experience: ￼
•	Restrooms: Public toilets are available at the concourse level, with the Circle Line station’s restroom receiving a 4-star rating for cleanliness .
•	Accessibility: The station is wheelchair-friendly, featuring lifts, ramps, and tactile guidance systems for the visually impaired .
•	Retail Options: Retail shops are located at Basement 1 and the NEL concourse (Basement 2), offering convenience for commuters . ￼ ￼

Crowd Levels:

Given its central location and interchange status, Dhoby Ghaut MRT Station experiences high foot traffic:
•	Weekdays: Peak hours (7:00 AM - 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM) see significant crowds due to office commuters.
•	Weekends: The station remains busy throughout the day, attracting shoppers and tourists exploring nearby attractions.

Conclusion:

Dhoby Ghaut MRT Station stands out as a vital nexus in Singapore’s MRT network, offering unparalleled connectivity, comprehensive facilities, and proximity to key attractions. Whether you’re commuting for work or exploring the city, this station ensures a seamless and convenient transit experience.

Dhoby Ghaut MRT station was first opened on 12th December 1987, bringing rail connectivity to Plaza Singapura located at the eastern end of the Orchard Road shopping belt. It gets its name from Dhobi Ghat, which means "washerman's place" in Hindi, in reference to people that used to wash their laundry from a clear stream in the area (now Stamford Canal) until the early 1900s. It is the first and only triple-line interchange MRT station in Singapore as of now until the opening of Outram Park and Marina Bay MRT stations on the Stage 3 of Thomson-East Coast line later in 2022. Originally on the North South MRT line, it interchanged with North East MRT line on 20 June 2003 as well as the Circle MRT line on 17 April 2010. It is also the nearest MRT station to Istana Park, Dhoby Ghaut Green, Cathay Green, The Cathay and The Istana (where the residence of the President of Singapore is located at). The bus stop near Dhoby Ghaut MRT Station along Orchard Road is the terminating point for Short Trip 7B, 190A and 972A and is one of the three Circle MRT line terminuses.

Dhoby Ghaut station sits on the site of a former Jewish cemetery, which was recorded to be established sometime between 1838 and 1841 and actually survived WWII; however, it only held out until 1983 when the land was repossessed by the Singapore government for redevelopment. The cemetery has since been relocated to Choa Chu Kang

Before the station was built, it was tentatively named Istana, after the Istana in the vicinity. Its current name, Dhoby Ghaut, was selected to reflect the area's heritage as a traditional Indian laundromat, Indian washermen (or dhobies). 'Dhobi' was named for the Indian laundromats formerly working at the station's current premises and 'Ghat' refers to the steps leading down to the canal where the dhobis would smack dry the clothes after washing.

The Amber Mansions,  Jewish cemetery and Sivan temple have been demolished as a result. On 14 October 1983, the contract 106, Singapore Pilling and Civil Engineering begin excavation of the tunnels from Somerset to City Hall together with Dhoby Ghaut MRT station, and was awarded. The other intermediate shafts are at Waterloo Street and at Victoria Street.

When Dhoby Ghaut station was under construction, there was a small cave-in at the Dhoby Ghaut MRT station which developed a hole 6m wide at Cathay Cinema on 12 January 1985, and a fatal accident happened in June 1985 due to a breach of safety rules. Construction for the North South Line was completed on 12 September 1985.

City Hall MRT Station (NS25/EW13) is one of Singapore’s most vital, high-traffic underground transit nodes. Serving as a crucial cross-platform interchange between the North South Line and the East West Line, the station’s brilliant two-tier layout allows thousands of daily commuters to switch lines effortlessly by simply walking across the platform, completely eliminating the need to change floors.
Situated squarely within the historic and civic heart of the Downtown Core, City Hall MRT functions as an expansive subterranean gateway. It links commuters directly to major commercial mega-malls, cultural landmarks, and administrative centers through a vast, air-conditioned network of underground walkways. Flawless Design: The stacked island platform design serves as a gold standard in transit planning, letting commuters switch between eastbound and northbound (or westbound and southbound) trains in seconds. Direct Underground Connectivity: Provides fully sheltered access to Raffles City Shopping Centre, Capitol Singapore, Funan, and the underground pedestrian street link to Esplanade MRT station.
Civic Gateway: Steps away from premier cultural institutions like the National Gallery Singapore

Meadowsfrom 1926 to 1929. A flight of stairs takes visitors from the Corinthian colonnade to the main building. The building was constructed to replace several houses designed by architect G.D. Coleman. It was first known as Municipal Building until 1951 when Singapore was granted city status by King George VI.

Raffles Place in Singapore is a captivating destination that effortlessly blends historical charm with contemporary vibrancy. Having explored this iconic neighborhood, it is with great pleasure that I award Raffles Place a well-deserved five-star rating.

The centerpiece of Raffles Place is the historic Raffles Place Park, named after Singapore's founding father, Sir Stamford Raffles. This lush green oasis provides a welcome respite amidst the bustling cityscape. The well-manicured lawns, tranquil ponds, and elegant statues create a serene ambiance, inviting visitors to unwind and appreciate the beauty of their surroundings.

The architectural marvels that line Raffles Place showcase the city's dynamic spirit and modernity. Skyscrapers tower above, housing global financial institutions and multinational corporations. The gleaming glass facades and innovative designs exemplify Singapore's status as a global financial hub. As I strolled through the streets, the juxtaposition of historic buildings and futuristic structures offered a unique visual tapestry, symbolizing the city's ability to blend tradition and progress seamlessly.

Raffles Place is not just a business district; it is a cultural and culinary haven. The neighborhood boasts a wide array of dining options that cater to every palate. From trendy cafes and fine dining establishments to local hawker centers, culinary delights await at every turn. Indulge in a gastronomic journey, savoring diverse cuisines from around the world or sampling delectable local dishes. The variety of dining choices ensures that every culinary craving is satisfied.

Shopaholics will find themselves in paradise at Raffles Place. The neighborhood is home to luxury boutiques, high-end malls, and unique specialty stores. From fashion and accessories to electronics and home decor, the retail offerings cater to a range of tastes and preferences. The experience of shopping in Raffles Place is elevated by the impeccable service and attention to detail that Singapore is renowned for.

Raffles Place is also a transportation hub, making it easily accessible from all corners of the city. The efficient MRT (Mass Rapid Transit) system connects Raffles Place to various parts of Singapore, ensuring convenient travel for both residents and visitors. The well-planned pedestrian walkways and underground passages further enhance accessibility, allowing for seamless exploration of the area.

Beyond its commercial prowess, Raffles Place holds historical significance. Marina Bay in Singapore is a stunning example of modern urban planning and architectural brilliance. Located at the heart of Singapore's downtown, it is a vibrant hub that perfectly encapsulates the city-state's blend of innovation, luxury, and cultural diversity.

One of the most iconic features of Marina Bay is the Marina Bay Sands, a massive integrated resort that dominates the skyline with its three towering structures connected by a unique rooftop SkyPark. The SkyPark offers breathtaking panoramic views of the city, especially at sunset when the skyline is bathed in a golden glow. The infinity pool at the top is also a must-visit, offering a surreal experience of swimming with the city at your feet.

The area around Marina Bay is equally impressive. The Marina Bay Promenade is a beautifully designed waterfront walk that provides scenic views of the bay and is a perfect spot for an evening stroll. The Merlion Park, featuring Singapore's iconic Merlion statue, is another highlight, drawing tourists and locals alike for photo opportunities and to enjoy the atmosphere.

For those interested in culture and the arts, the ArtScience Museum, with its lotus-inspired design, offers a range of exhibitions that blend art, science, and technology. The Marina Bay Sands itself houses numerous high-end shops, restaurants, and a world-class casino, catering to every kind of luxury experience.

The Gardens by the Bay, located just a short walk away, is a futuristic garden space with towering Supertree structures that light up beautifully at night. The Cloud Forest and Flower Dome within the gardens are also spectacular, offering a unique blend of nature and technology.

Transportation in and around Marina Bay is seamless, with excellent connectivity via the MRT and buses. The area is also pedestrian-friendly, making it easy to explore on foot.

Overall, Marina Bay is a must-visit destination in Singapore, offering a mix of luxury, culture, and breathtaking views that make it one of the most memorable places in the city. Whether you're there for shopping, dining, sightseeing, or just soaking in the vibrant atmosphere, Marina Bay has something for everyone.

Opened on 23 November 2014 as part of the southern terminus of the North South MRT Line, the station was first announced in the 2008 Land Transport Master Plan, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) announced a 1-kilometre (0.62 mi) extension of the NSL from Marina Bay to provide connectivity to future developments in the area, as well as to the Marina Bay Cruise Centre. Construction of the station had started in December 2009 which involved the challenge of cutting underneath a section of the Marina Coastal Expressway (MCE) and it was completed in September 2014 after nearly five years. The station had its opening ceremony on 22 November 2014, a day before its official opening. This station is located underneath Marina Coastal Drive near Marina South Pier (which offers ferry services to the Southern Islands (St. John's Island, Lazarus Island and Kusu Island)) and Marina Bay Cruise Centre and was named after the nearby ferry pier terminal, bringing rail connectivity to serve the seaside areas at Marina South. It is also served by SBS Transit bus service 400 which connects Shenton Way Bus Terminal with Marina Bay Cruise Centre along Marina Coastal Drive via Cecil Street, Marina Boulevard, Marina Gardens Drive (Gardens by the Bay), Central Boulevard (Marina Bay MRT station), Straits View (Downtown MRT station) and Park Street (Shenton Way MRT station).
